prompt: Create ONE independent professional educational textbook plate for the single story 'Microsoft redesigns Copilot around Home, Code, and persistent Autopilot'. This is the complete isolated brief; depict no other article, status dashboard or edition content. White background, exactly 1200x630 intended canvas, wide composition, 40px safe margins, refined navy serif title and concise navy sans-serif labels, restrained blue/copper/teal. Design three distinct horizontal swimlanes within a cohesive page, organized by type of work and time: top lane HOME has a detailed annotated document with notes and evidence snippets, a two-way conversation motif and a human review margin; middle lane CODE has a small natural-language specification turning into an editable application schematic, code cells and a test/preview inset; bottom lane AUTOPILOT has a persistent task envelope crossing a time ribbon with 'Start', 'Checkpoint', 'Resume', 'Review', showing durable state as stacked task cards and a clear stop/approval control. The third lane should visually show continuity over time, not a simple row of icons. A small left decision fork asks 'Discuss', 'Build' or 'Delegate', and routes to its matching lane. Each lane ends in a concrete conceptual output: 'Reviewed draft', 'Reusable artifact', 'Reviewed task result'. Right margin contains a shared review bracket with 'Permissions', 'Data scope', 'Approval', 'Audit' labeled 'Controls to verify'. Title exactly 'Three modes of AI work'. Label the three lanes exactly 'HOME — interactive work', 'CODE — build solutions', 'AUTOPILOT — persistent work'. Footer 'Conceptual workflow guide — availability, rollout and controls vary'. At least 10 meaningful story-specific components, subtle depth and fine annotation leader lines, sophisticated editorial page design, no decorative collage. All text legible and no overlap. No people or physical office props, no branded product screenshots, no invented capabilities or statistics, no completion dashboard, no image reuse.
